svg.text: A row that lost is not a row that could not measure.
The log prints the reason under each FAIL, so it can tell the two apart. The CSV carried notes alone, so it could not.
Today every row gets a third verdict column: the notes refused as MeasurementUnsound.

g.text: load claims_ok claims_failed
200 rps 12 the tail did not get worse
400 rps 12 the tail did not get worse
what the log said under each:
200: ITL p99 is 9.1 ms against 7.8 ms
400: no frame gaps to compare
same note, same cell, one is a result and one is noise

svg.text: the two refusals a gate raises

g.text: AcceptanceFailure
The run measured what it set out to, and the
answer was no. The numbers are good: they say
the capture lost. Keep the row, read the verdict.
MeasurementUnsound
The run could not measure it: too few gaps,
a dropped request, arms that served other work.
The numbers are not a result. Drop the row.
"claims_ok": count of exc is None
"claims_failed": "; ".join(note, exc is not None)
"claims_unsound": "; ".join(note, MeasurementUnsound)
a subset of claims_failed, in print order
last, so Day 76's header is still a prefix
the table still reads held/total, nothing counted twice
_delta at floor 20: unsound ""
_delta at floor 1000: unsound "the arms are comparable"
toy sweep smoke: every row's unsound cell is empty

svg.text: how a card sweep's notebook reads it

g.text: 1. drop what cannot be used
rows = rows[rows.claims_unsound == ""]
2. then read what is left
lost = rows[rows.claims_failed != ""]
A plot that kept an unsound row would be plotting
a run that never measured the thing on its axis.
the CSV now says what the log says, reason included
